english: I don’t want the mortgage to leave me financially strangled.
context: BUYING A HOME — VERY RELEVANT TO YOU — Buying a home: not wanting mortgage repayments to leave you financially squeezed.

foreign: Je veux qu’on garde de la marge.
english: I want us to keep some financial breathing room.
context: BUYING A HOME — VERY RELEVANT TO YOU — Buying a home: wanting enough monthly financial breathing room after the mortgage.

foreign: Je veux pas acheter au maximum de ce que la banque nous prête.
english: I don’t want to buy at the absolute maximum the bank will lend us.
context: BUYING A HOME — VERY RELEVANT TO YOU — Buying a home: not wanting to spend the absolute maximum the bank is willing to lend.

foreign: Faut rajouter les frais de notaire.
english: You have to add the notary fees.

lemmas.english: notary/conveyancing fees on a property purchase

context: BUYING A HOME — VERY RELEVANT TO YOU

foreign: Ça fait vite grimper le budget.
english: That pushes the budget up quickly.
context: BUYING A HOME — VERY RELEVANT TO YOU — Buying a home: referring to extra purchase costs such as notary fees pushing the total budget up.

foreign: Elle a hérité de combien ?
english: How much did she inherit?

foreign: Il a hérité de la maison.
english: He inherited the house.

foreign: Elle a touché un héritage.
english: She received an inheritance.

foreign: Ils ont partagé l’héritage.
english: They divided the inheritance.

foreign: Il faudrait racheter la part des autres.
english: They’d have to buy out everyone else’s share.
context: INHERITANCE — HÉRITAGE / SUCCESSION — Inheritance: one heir would need to buy the other heirs' shares of inherited property.

foreign: Il y a des droits de succession à payer.
english: There’s inheritance tax to pay.

foreign: La succession est toujours pas réglée.
english: The estate still hasn’t been settled.

foreign: C’est le notaire qui s’en occupe.
english: The notary is dealing with it.

lemmas.english: notary; French legal professional handling property/estates

context: INHERITANCE — HÉRITAGE / SUCCESSION — Inheritance/succession: the notaire is handling the estate.

foreign: Je vous appelle au sujet de la succession de ma mère.
english: I’m calling regarding my mother’s estate.

foreign: Tu comptes partir à la retraite quand ?
english: When are you planning to retire?

foreign: T’as regardé combien tu toucherais à la retraite ?
english: Have you looked at how much you’d get in retirement?

foreign: Faudrait que je regarde mon relevé de carrière.
english: I should check my career record.

lemmas.english: career contribution record for French pension rights

foreign: Il me manque des trimestres.
english: I’m missing some qualifying pension quarters.
context: RETIREMENT / PENSIONS — LA RETRAITE — French pension: referring to missing qualifying pension quarters/trimestres.

foreign: Cette période apparaît pas.
english: That period isn’t showing.
context: RETIREMENT / PENSIONS — LA RETRAITE — French pension record: a period of work or contributions is missing from the relevé de carrière.

foreign: Tu peux me prêter un peu d’argent ?
english: Can you lend me some money?

foreign: Tu pourrais me prêter 100 euros jusqu’à la fin du mois ?
english: Could you lend me €100 until the end of the month?

foreign: Je te rembourse dès que je suis payée.
english: I’ll pay you back as soon as I’m paid.

foreign: Rembourse-moi quand tu peux.
english: Pay me back when you can.

foreign: Je préfère qu’on soit clairs dès le départ.
english: I’d rather we’re clear from the start.
context: LENDING MONEY TO FAMILY — Lending money to family/friends: wanting repayment expectations to be clear from the start.

foreign: Je veux pas que l’argent crée des histoires entre nous.
english: I don’t want money creating problems between us.
context: LENDING MONEY TO FAMILY — Lending money to family/friends: worrying that money could create conflict between you.

foreign: Il me doit toujours de l’argent.
english: He still owes me money.
context: LENDING MONEY TO FAMILY — Lending money to family/friends: someone still owes you money.

foreign: Je veux bien aider, mais faut pas abuser.
english: I’m happy to help, but don’t take the piss.
context: LENDING MONEY TO FAMILY — Lending money to family/friends: willing to help financially, but not to be taken advantage of.

foreign: Je te rends ça demain.
english: I’ll pay you back tomorrow.
context: BORROWING BETWEEN FRIENDS — Paying back money you borrowed from someone.

foreign: On est quittes, laisse tomber.
english: We’re even, forget it.
context: BORROWING BETWEEN FRIENDS — Small debts between friends: saying neither person owes the other anything now.

foreign: T’es sûre que ça te met pas dans la galère ?
english: Are you sure that won’t leave you short?
context: BORROWING BETWEEN FRIENDS — Before lending money to a friend/family member: checking that lending it will not leave them short.

foreign: Ça me gêne de réclamer mon propre argent.
english: I feel awkward asking for my own money back.
context: WHEN SOMEONE DOESN'T PAY YOU BACK — Someone still owes you money, and you feel awkward having to ask for it back.

foreign: S’il peut pas tout rendre d’un coup, qu’il me le dise.
english: If he can’t repay it all at once, he should tell me.
context: WHEN SOMEONE DOESN'T PAY YOU BACK — Someone owes you money: saying they should tell you if they cannot repay it all in one go.

foreign: Ils te proposent combien ?
english: How much are they offering you?
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation/job offer: asking how much the employer is offering.

foreign: T’as demandé combien ?
english: How much did you ask for?
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: asking what salary amount the person requested.

foreign: Tu vas négocier ?
english: Are you going to negotiate?
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: asking whether the person plans to negotiate the offer.

foreign: Ils peuvent clairement faire mieux.
english: They can clearly do better.
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: saying the employer can offer more money.

foreign: C’est combien en net ?
english: How much is that net?
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary discussion: asking what the amount works out to after deductions.

foreign: Brut ou net ?
english: Gross or net?
context: IS IT RUDE TO ASK? — Salary discussion: clarifying whether a stated figure is gross or net.

foreign: Ils ont fait une contre-proposition.
english: They made a counteroffer.
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: the employer has responded with a different salary offer.

foreign: Ils veulent pas bouger sur le salaire.
english: They won’t budge on salary.
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: the employer will not increase the salary offer.

foreign: J’aimerais qu’on puisse rediscuter de la rémunération.
english: I’d like us to discuss the salary again.

foreign: Au vu de mon expérience, j’espérais plutôt X.
english: Given my experience, I was hoping for more like X.
context: NEGOTIATING SALARY — Salary negotiation: professionally stating the salary you were hoping for based on your experience.

foreign: Il y a une marge de négociation sur le salaire ?
english: Is there any room for negotiation on salary?

foreign: Tu factures combien ?
english: How much do you charge?

foreign: C’est quoi ton tarif ?
english: What’s your rate?

foreign: Je sais jamais combien demander.
english: I never know how much to charge.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: deciding what rate to quote a client.

foreign: Faut arrêter de bosser gratuitement.
english: I need to stop working for free.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: realising you should not keep doing professional work for free.

foreign: Si je compte le temps passé dessus, c’est même pas rentable.
english: If I count the time I spent on it, it’s not even profitable.

foreign: Ils m’ont demandé un devis.
english: They asked me for a quote.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: a client has asked you to provide a quote.

foreign: Je facture à la journée.
english: I charge by the day.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: stating that your rate is charged per day.

foreign: Je facture à l’heure.
english: I charge hourly.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: stating that your rate is charged per hour.

foreign: Je fais un forfait.
english: I charge a flat fee.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance/creative work: offering a fixed/package fee rather than hourly billing.

foreign: Les modifications sont comprises jusqu’à…
english: Revisions are included up to…
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance quote: specifying how many revisions are included in the agreed fee.

foreign: Au-delà, je facture en plus.
english: Beyond that, I charge extra.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance quote: saying additional revisions/work beyond the agreed scope will cost extra.

foreign: Ils veulent les droits aussi ?
english: Do they want the rights as well?
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Creative freelance work: asking whether the client also wants usage/copyright rights, which may change the fee.

foreign: La facture est arrivée à échéance.
english: The invoice is due.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance invoice: the payment due date has arrived.

foreign: Faut que je les relance.
english: I need to chase them.
context: FREELANCE / CREATIVE INCOME — Freelance invoice: you need to chase the client because payment is due or late.

foreign: Je veux pas brader mon travail.
english: I don’t want to undervalue my work.

foreign: Tu crois que je peux le vendre combien ?
english: How much do you think I could sell it for?

foreign: Regarde combien ça part d’occasion.
english: See how much they go for second-hand.

foreign: Je l’ai mis à 80.
english: I listed it for €80.
context: SELLING SECOND-HAND — Selling second-hand: you have listed the item at €80.

foreign: Je l’ai mis un peu plus cher pour pouvoir négocier.
english: I listed it a bit higher so there’s room to negotiate.
context: SELLING SECOND-HAND — Selling second-hand: you listed slightly high so there would be room for buyers to negotiate.

foreign: À ce prix-là, je préfère le garder.
english: At that price, I’d rather keep it.
context: SELLING SECOND-HAND — Selling second-hand: the offers are so low that you would rather keep the item.

foreign: Il est quasiment neuf.
english: It’s practically new.

foreign: Il a quelques traces d’usure.
english: It has a few signs of wear.

foreign: Bonjour, c’est toujours disponible ?
english: Hi, is this still available?
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: a buyer is asking whether the item is still for sale.

foreign: Vous le feriez à 50 € ?
english: Would you take €50?
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: a buyer is making a lower offer.

foreign: Quel est votre dernier prix ?
english: What’s your lowest price?
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: a buyer is asking for the seller's lowest acceptable price.

foreign: Le prix est négociable ?
english: Is the price negotiable?
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: a buyer is asking whether the asking price can be negotiated.

foreign: Je peux venir le chercher aujourd’hui.
english: I can collect it today.
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: a buyer is offering to collect the item today.

foreign: Le prix est ferme.
english: The price is firm.
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: the seller is saying they will not negotiate the price.

foreign: Je peux faire 70, mais pas moins.
english: I can do €70, but no lower.
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: the seller is giving their lowest acceptable price.

foreign: Premier arrivé, premier servi.
english: First come, first served.
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand listing: the seller will give the item to whoever commits/collects first.

foreign: Pas d’envoi, remise en main propre uniquement.
english: No postage, in-person handover only.
context: LEBONCOIN HAGGLING — Leboncoin/second-hand sale: the seller will not post the item; collection/in-person handover only.

foreign: Tu l’as mis sur Vinted ?
english: Did you put it on Vinted?

foreign: Il est neuf avec étiquette.
english: It’s new with tags.
context: VINTED — Vinted/second-hand listing: describing an item as new with tags.

foreign: J’ai fait une offre.
english: I made an offer.
context: VINTED — Vinted: you have sent the seller a lower-price offer.

foreign: Elle a fait une contre-offre.
english: She countered.
context: VINTED — Vinted: the seller has replied to your offer with a different price.

foreign: Avec les frais, ça revient presque au prix neuf.
english: With the fees, it almost works out at the new price.
context: VINTED — Vinted: once buyer protection/postage fees are added, the second-hand item is almost as expensive as buying it new.

foreign: Ça sent l’arnaque.
english: It smells like a scam.

foreign: Ça a l’air louche.
english: It looks dodgy.

foreign: C’est trop beau pour être vrai.
english: It’s too good to be true.

foreign: Donne pas tes coordonnées bancaires.
english: Don’t give them your bank details.

foreign: Je me suis fait avoir.
english: I got conned.

lemmas.english: to get conned; to get ripped off; to be fooled

foreign: Y a un paiement que je reconnais pas.
english: There’s a payment I don’t recognise.
context: SCAMS — ARNAQUES — Possible card fraud: there is a payment on the account that you do not recognise.

foreign: Fais opposition à la carte.
english: Block/cancel the card.

lemmas.english: to block/cancel a bank card or payment instrument

context: SCAMS — ARNAQUES — Possible card fraud: telling someone to block/cancel the bank card.

foreign: L’assurance prend en charge ?
english: Does insurance cover it?

foreign: Il y a une franchise.
english: There’s an excess/deductible.
context: INSURANCE — ASSURANCE — Insurance claim: referring to the deductible/excess you must pay yourself.

foreign: Faut faire une déclaration de sinistre.
english: We need to file an insurance claim.

foreign: Ils vont envoyer un expert.
english: They’re sending an assessor.
context: INSURANCE — ASSURANCE — Insurance claim: the insurer is sending an expert/assessor to inspect the damage or loss.

foreign: C’est remboursé par la Sécu ?
english: Is it reimbursed by Social Security?

foreign: Et la mutuelle prend le reste ?
english: And does the supplementary insurer cover the rest?

foreign: Ça a été télétransmis ?
english: Was it transmitted electronically?
context: MUTUELLE / HEALTH REIMBURSEMENTS — French healthcare reimbursement: asking whether the claim was electronically transmitted between the healthcare system and insurer.

foreign: Il reste combien à ma charge ?
english: How much do I still have to pay myself?
context: MUTUELLE / HEALTH REIMBURSEMENTS — French healthcare reimbursement: asking how much remains for you to pay out of pocket.

foreign: J’ai eu 40 euros de reste à charge.
english: I had €40 left to pay out of pocket.

foreign: Je vais leur envoyer le décompte.
english: I’ll send them the reimbursement statement.
context: MUTUELLE / HEALTH REIMBURSEMENTS — French healthcare reimbursement: sending the reimbursement statement to the mutuelle.

foreign: J’ai pris une prune.
english: I got a parking ticket.

foreign: J’ai dépassé de dix minutes.
english: I overstayed by ten minutes.
context: PARKING FINES — AMENDES DE STATIONNEMENT — Parking: you stayed ten minutes beyond the paid/allowed parking time.

foreign: Je vais la contester.
english: I’m going to appeal it.
context: PARKING FINES — AMENDES DE STATIONNEMENT — Parking fine: you are going to challenge/appeal the ticket.

foreign: J’ai oublié de payer et maintenant c’est majoré.
english: I forgot to pay and now it’s increased.
context: PARKING FINES — AMENDES DE STATIONNEMENT — Parking fine: you paid late and the fine has now been increased.

foreign: Je crois que je me suis fait flasher.
english: I think I got flashed by a speed camera.

lemmas.english: to get caught/flashed by a speed camera

foreign: Tu vas perdre des points ?
english: Are you going to lose points?
context: SPEEDING FINES — Speeding: asking whether the offence will cost points on the French driving licence.

foreign: Ils m’ont retiré un point.
english: They took a point off my licence.

foreign: Fais gaffe, y a un radar là.
english: Careful, there’s a speed camera there.

foreign: On fait comment pour les dépenses ?
english: How are we doing expenses?
context: SPLITTING HOLIDAY COSTS — Holiday with other people: deciding how shared expenses will be divided.

foreign: On réglera les comptes à la fin.
english: We’ll settle up at the end.
context: SPLITTING HOLIDAY COSTS — Holiday with other people: planning to settle everyone's shared expenses at the end.

foreign: Note qui a payé quoi.
english: Note who paid for what.
context: SPLITTING HOLIDAY COSTS — Holiday with other people: keeping track of who paid each shared expense.

foreign: Il faut rajouter l’essence.
english: We need to add petrol.
context: SPLITTING HOLIDAY COSTS — Splitting holiday costs: remembering to add fuel/petrol to the shared expenses.

foreign: Et les péages.
english: And tolls.
context: SPLITTING HOLIDAY COSTS — Splitting holiday costs: remembering to add motorway tolls to the shared expenses.

foreign: Ils demandent une caution ?
english: Do they want a deposit?
context: AIRBNB / HOLIDAY RENTAL DEPOSITS — Airbnb/holiday rental: asking whether the host requires a security deposit.

foreign: Elle est débitée ou juste bloquée ?
english: Is it charged or just held?
context: AIRBNB / HOLIDAY RENTAL DEPOSITS — Airbnb/holiday rental security deposit: asking whether the amount is actually taken or only temporarily held.

foreign: Ils nous ont facturé des frais de ménage.
english: They charged us a cleaning fee.
context: AIRBNB / HOLIDAY RENTAL DEPOSITS — Holiday rental/Airbnb: the host/platform has charged an additional cleaning fee.

foreign: La formule du midi vaut le coup.
english: The lunchtime set menu is good value.

foreign: On donne combien ?
english: How much are we giving?
context: WEDDING GIFTS — Wedding gift: deciding how much money to give the couple.

foreign: Ils ont une liste de mariage ?
english: Do they have a wedding list?

foreign: Ils ont fait une cagnotte pour le voyage de noces.
english: They’ve made a honeymoon fund.

foreign: On met combien dans la carte ?
english: How much do we put in the card?
context: CHILDREN'S BIRTHDAY PARTY MONEY — Child's birthday party: deciding how much money to put inside the birthday card.

foreign: On lui donnera de l’argent de poche à quel âge ?
english: What age will we start giving him pocket money?

foreign: Tu veux garder tes sous ou les dépenser ?
english: Do you want to save your money or spend it?

foreign: C’est ton argent, c’est toi qui choisis.
english: It’s your money; you choose.

foreign: J’ai rendez-vous avec ma conseillère.
english: I’ve got an appointment with my bank adviser.
context: THE BANK — Banking: referring to an appointment with your female bank adviser.

foreign: Ils veulent des relevés de compte.
english: They want bank statements.
context: THE BANK — Banking/admin: the bank is asking you to provide bank statements.

foreign: Ils veulent mes bulletins de salaire.
english: They want my payslips.
context: THE BANK — Banking/admin: the bank is asking you to provide payslips.

foreign: Je voudrais augmenter mon plafond de carte.
english: I’d like to increase my card limit.
context: THE BANK — Banking: asking the bank to raise the card payment limit.

foreign: Je voudrais fermer ce compte.
english: I’d like to close this account.
context: THE BANK — Banking: asking to close a bank account.

foreign: T’as pris un crédit pour ça ?
english: Did you take out a loan for that?

foreign: Il me reste combien à rembourser ?
english: How much have I got left to repay?
context: CREDIT CARDS / LOANS / DEBT — Loan: asking how much of the borrowed amount is still outstanding.

foreign: Je rembourse X par mois.
english: I repay X a month.
context: CREDIT CARDS / LOANS / DEBT — Loan: stating the monthly repayment amount.

foreign: J’ai pas envie de m’endetter pour ça.
english: I don’t want to get into debt for that.

foreign: Je veux solder le prêt.
english: I want to pay off the loan.

foreign: Elle a combien de kilomètres ?
english: How many kilometres has it done?
context: BUYING A CAR — Buying a used car: asking about the car's mileage.

foreign: Et niveau entretien ?
english: What about maintenance costs?
context: BUYING A CAR — Buying a used car: asking about maintenance/running costs and servicing.

foreign: Il faut prévoir le contrôle technique.
english: We need to factor in the roadworthiness inspection.

foreign: La courroie a été faite ?
english: Has the timing belt been done?
context: BUYING A CAR — Buying a used car: asking whether the timing belt has already been replaced/serviced.

foreign: Vous avez les factures d’entretien ?
english: Do you have the maintenance receipts?
context: BUYING A CAR — Buying a used car: asking the seller for the vehicle's maintenance/service invoices.

foreign: Fais faire un devis.
english: Get a quote.
context: REPAIRS / TRADESPEOPLE — Home repair/tradesperson: advising someone to get a written quote before agreeing to the work.

foreign: La main-d’œuvre est à combien ?
english: How much is labour?
context: REPAIRS / TRADESPEOPLE — Home repair/tradesperson: asking how much of the quote is labour.

foreign: Il faut payer un acompte ?
english: Do we need to pay a deposit?
context: REPAIRS / TRADESPEOPLE — Home repair/tradesperson: asking whether an upfront deposit is required before work begins.

foreign: Je paie rien tant que j’ai pas le devis.
english: I’m paying nothing until I have the quote.
context: REPAIRS / TRADESPEOPLE — Home repair/tradesperson: refusing to pay before receiving the quote.

foreign: Le plombier est passé.
english: The plumber came.
context: HOW THE FUCK DID THE PLUMBER COST THAT MUCH? — Plumbing repair: the plumber has just come to do the work.

foreign: Quatre cent cinquante balles pour une heure ?!
english: Four hundred and fifty euros for one hour?!
context: HOW THE FUCK DID THE PLUMBER COST THAT MUCH? — Plumbing repair: reacting to being charged €450 for one hour of work.

foreign: Mais il a réparé quoi, le réseau d’eau de toute la France ?
english: What did he repair, France’s entire water system?!
context: HOW THE FUCK DID THE PLUMBER COST THAT MUCH? — Plumbing repair: joking that the plumber's huge bill looks as if he repaired the entire French water network.

foreign: Il a des mains en or ou quoi ?
english: Are his hands made of gold or what?
context: HOW THE FUCK DID THE PLUMBER COST THAT MUCH? — Plumbing repair: joking about the plumber's very high labour charge.

foreign: T’as reçu le devis ?
english: Did you get the quote?
context: THE SACRED DEVIS — Home repair: asking whether the tradesperson's quote has arrived.

foreign: Y a quoi dans ce devis exactement ?
english: What exactly is included in this quote?
context: THE SACRED DEVIS — Home repair quote: asking exactly what work/items are included in the devis.

foreign: C’est détaillé ?
english: Is it itemised?
context: THE SACRED DEVIS — Home repair quote: asking whether the costs are itemised in detail.

foreign: Vous pouvez me détailler ce poste ?
english: Could you break down this item for me?
context: THE SACRED DEVIS — Home repair quote: politely asking the tradesperson/company to explain one line item.

foreign: Vous pourriez revoir le tarif ?
english: Could you reconsider the price?
context: THE SACRED DEVIS — Home repair quote: politely asking whether they can reduce/reconsider the quoted price.

foreign: Je crois qu’on m’a surfacturée.
english: I think I’ve been overcharged.

foreign: C’était pas dans le devis.
english: That wasn’t in the quote.
context: BEING OVERCHARGED — Being overcharged after work/service: the final charge includes something that was not in the agreed quote.

foreign: Pourquoi il y a 80 euros en plus ?
english: Why is there an extra €80?
context: BEING OVERCHARGED — Being overcharged after work/service: questioning an extra €80 added to the expected amount.

foreign: Je constate un écart entre le devis et la facture.
english: I can see a discrepancy between the quote and invoice.

foreign: Vous pouvez m’expliquer à quoi correspondent ces frais supplémentaires ?
english: Could you explain these additional charges?

foreign: Vous pourriez faire un geste ?
english: Could you give me a discount?
context: NEGOTIATING PRICES GENERALLY — Price negotiation: politely asking for a goodwill discount or price reduction.

foreign: C’est votre meilleur prix ?
english: Is that your best price?

foreign: Si je prends les deux, vous pouvez faire un prix ?
english: If I take both, can you give me a deal?

foreign: Je veux résilier.
english: I want to cancel.
context: CANCELLING CONTRACTS / SUBSCRIPTIONS — Cancelling a contract or subscription.

foreign: Il reste combien de mois d’engagement ?
english: How many months are left on the contract?
context: CANCELLING CONTRACTS / SUBSCRIPTIONS — Cancelling a contract/subscription: asking how long remains in the minimum commitment period.

foreign: Y a des frais de résiliation ?
english: Is there a cancellation fee?

foreign: Ils m’ont proposé une réduction pour que je reste.
english: They offered me a discount to stay.
context: CANCELLING CONTRACTS / SUBSCRIPTIONS — Cancelling a contract/subscription: the company offered a discount to persuade you not to leave.

foreign: Je souhaite recevoir une confirmation écrite.
english: I’d like written confirmation.
context: CANCELLING CONTRACTS / SUBSCRIPTIONS — Cancelling a contract/subscription: asking for written proof that the cancellation has been processed.

foreign: Tu sais combien il gagne ?
english: Do you know how much he earns?

foreign: Il gagne bien sa vie.
english: He earns good money.

foreign: Ça gagne combien dans ce métier ?
english: What do people earn in that job?

foreign: Ça se fait de demander combien elle gagne ?
english: Is it okay to ask how much she earns?
context: IS IT RUDE TO ASK? — Talking about salary: asking whether it is socially acceptable to ask what someone earns.

foreign: Je préfère pas dire exactement.
english: I’d rather not say exactly.

english: I received daily sickness benefit payments.

context: SICK PAY / SALARY ADMIN — Salary admin: something on this month's payslip looks wrong or unusual.

english: What is this deduction?
context: SICK PAY / SALARY ADMIN — Salary admin: asking what a particular deduction on the payslip is.

english: They owe me back pay.
context: SICK PAY / SALARY ADMIN — Salary admin: the employer owes back pay from an earlier underpayment.

foreign: Il manque des heures sup.
english: Some overtime hours are missing.
context: SICK PAY / SALARY ADMIN — Salary admin: overtime hours are missing from the payslip/pay calculation.

foreign: Je toucherai combien pendant le congé maternité ?
english: How much will I get during maternity leave?

foreign: La déclaration de grossesse a bien été prise en compte ?
english: Has the pregnancy declaration been processed?
context: MATERNITY LEAVE MONEY — Maternity admin: checking that the official pregnancy declaration has been processed.

foreign: On pourrait se permettre que je prenne un congé parental ?
english: Could we afford for me to take parental leave?
context: PARENTAL LEAVE MONEY — Household finances: deciding whether you can afford for one parent to take parental leave.

foreign: On a droit à une aide pour la garde ?
english: Are we entitled to childcare support?

english: Is it calculated according to the family quotient?

context: MONEY + CHILDREN — French childcare costs: asking whether the fee/subsidy is based on the household quotient familial.

context: CHILDCARE SUBSIDIES — Childcare subsidy: asking how much childcare still costs after the assistance is applied.

english: I have a meal-voucher card.

english: Do you take meal vouchers?
context: TITRES-RESTAURANT / TICKETS RESTO — At a restaurant/shop: asking whether they accept French titres-restaurant/meal vouchers.

foreign: T’as des chèques vacances ?
english: Do you get holiday vouchers?
context: EMPLOYEE BENEFITS — AVANTAGES — Employee benefits: asking whether the job includes French chèques-vacances/holiday vouchers.

context: EMPLOYEE BENEFITS — AVANTAGES — Employee benefits/pay: asking whether there will be a bonus this year.

english: Is there a profit-sharing incentive?
context: EMPLOYEE BENEFITS — AVANTAGES — Work benefits: asking whether the employer offers an intéressement profit-sharing incentive.

foreign: Il y a de la participation ?
english: Is there employee profit-sharing?
context: EMPLOYEE BENEFITS — AVANTAGES — Work benefits: asking whether the employer has the French participation profit-sharing scheme.

foreign: Faut que je fasse ma note de frais.
english: I need to submit my expense claim.
context: EXPENSE CLAIMS — NOTES DE FRAIS — Work expenses: you need to submit your expense claim.

foreign: Je dois rentrer les frais kilométriques.
english: I need to enter the mileage expenses.
context: EXPENSE CLAIMS — NOTES DE FRAIS — Work expenses: entering mileage expenses for reimbursement.

foreign: J’attends toujours le remboursement de ma note de frais.
english: I’m still waiting for my expense reimbursement.
context: EXPENSE CLAIMS — NOTES DE FRAIS — Work expenses: waiting for the employer to reimburse an already-submitted expense claim.

foreign: J’ai reçu une relance.
english: I received a payment reminder.
context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt/payment admin: you have received a reminder saying money is still owed.

foreign: Ils m’ont envoyé une mise en demeure.
english: They sent me a formal demand.
context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt collection: you have received a formal demand to pay/comply.

english: They passed the case to debt collection.

lemmas.english: debt collection; recovery of money owed

context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt collection: the unpaid/disputed account has been passed to a collection service.

foreign: Je conteste cette somme.
english: I dispute this amount.
context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt collection/billing dispute: formally saying you dispute the amount being claimed.

foreign: Cette facture a déjà été réglée.
english: This invoice has already been paid.
context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt collection/billing dispute: stating that the invoice has already been paid.

foreign: Je peux vous transmettre la preuve de paiement.
english: I can send you proof of payment.
context: DEBT COLLECTION — RECOUVREMENT — Debt collection/billing dispute: offering proof that the payment was made.

english: I received a letter from a judicial officer.

lemmas.english: French judicial officer (modern term replacing huissier)

context: BAILIFFS — COMMISSAIRES DE JUSTICE — Debt enforcement: you have received correspondence from a French commissaire de justice.

foreign: Un huissier ?
english: A bailiff?
context: BAILIFFS — COMMISSAIRES DE JUSTICE — Debt enforcement: reacting to 'commissaire de justice' with the older/common word 'huissier'.

foreign: J’ai reçu une sommation.
english: I received a formal demand.
context: BAILIFFS — COMMISSAIRES DE JUSTICE — Debt enforcement: you have received a formal demand/summons.

foreign: Je peux pas payer tout d’un coup.
english: I can’t pay it all at once.
context: BAILIFFS — COMMISSAIRES DE JUSTICE — Debt repayment: saying you cannot pay the whole amount in one payment.

foreign: J’ai fait un don.
english: I made a donation.

foreign: C’est déductible des impôts ?
english: Is it tax-deductible?
context: DONATIONS / CHARITY — Charitable donation in France: asking whether the donation qualifies for a tax deduction.

foreign: Ils envoient un reçu fiscal.
english: They send a tax receipt.
context: DONATIONS / CHARITY — Charitable donation in France: referring to the tax certificate/receipt used for the deduction.

foreign: Ils ont fait une cagnotte.
english: They started a fundraising pot.
context: FUNDRAISING POTS — CAGNOTTES — Fundraising: someone has created an online/shared cagnotte for people to contribute money.

foreign: L’objectif est presque atteint.
english: The target has nearly been reached.
context: FUNDRAISING POTS — CAGNOTTES — Fundraising: the cagnotte is close to its target amount.

foreign: On se fixe un budget pour Noël ?
english: Shall we set a Christmas budget?

foreign: On pourrait faire un Secret Santa.
english: We could do Secret Santa.
context: CHRISTMAS BUDGETING — Christmas gifts: suggesting Secret Santa to reduce the number/cost of gifts.

foreign: J’essaie d’étaler les dépenses.
english: I’m trying to spread the spending out.
context: CHRISTMAS BUDGETING — Christmas budgeting: buying gifts over time so December is not one huge expense.

foreign: Je vais lui mettre un peu d’argent de côté.
english: I’m going to put some money aside for him.
context: GIVING MONEY TO CHILDREN / GRANDCHILDREN — Saving for a child/grandchild: putting money aside in their name/for their future.

foreign: Même une petite somme, sur des années ça monte.
english: Even a small amount grows over the years.
context: GIVING MONEY TO CHILDREN / GRANDCHILDREN — Saving for a child/grandchild: noting that regular small amounts can build up over many years.

english: Did he have funeral insurance?

english: Are there crematorium fees?

english: What are we doing with the joint account?
context: SEPARATION / DIVORCE — SEPARATING FINANCES — Separation/divorce: deciding what to do with the joint bank account.

foreign: Cette dette est à qui ?
english: Whose debt is this?
context: SEPARATION / DIVORCE — SEPARATING FINANCES — Separation/divorce: working out which partner is responsible for a debt.

foreign: On fait quoi de l’épargne commune ?
english: What are we doing with the joint savings?
context: SEPARATION / DIVORCE — SEPARATING FINANCES — Separation/divorce: deciding how to divide or handle joint savings.

english: Shall we put it up for sale?
context: SELLING A HOUSE — Selling a house/property: deciding whether to put it on the market.

english: We need to get a valuation.

english: I can see two identical debits on my account.

english: It seems the payment was taken twice.

english: Why is it still pending?

foreign: C’est marqué « paiement en attente ».
english: It says “payment pending”.

english: It still reduced my available balance.

english: It might be a pre-authorisation.
context: CARD PAYMENT “PENDING” FOR DAYS — Pending card payment: suggesting the amount may only be a temporary pre-authorisation.

english: I have two pending authorisations.
context: CARD PAYMENT “PENDING” FOR DAYS — Pending card payment: two separate authorisation holds are showing for the transaction.

foreign: J’aime pas avoir 300 balles dans les limbes bancaires.
english: I don’t like having €300 in banking limbo.
context: CARD PAYMENT “PENDING” FOR DAYS — Pending card payment: joking about money being temporarily stuck/unavailable because of bank authorisations.

foreign: Le distributeur m’a débité mais il m’a pas donné l’argent.
english: The ATM debited me but didn’t give me the cash.
context: ATM PROBLEMS — ATM problem: the account was debited even though the cash machine did not dispense the money.

foreign: Il a avalé ma carte !
english: It swallowed my card!

context: ATM PROBLEMS — ATM problem: the cash machine has retained your bank card.

foreign: J’ai dépassé mon plafond de retrait.
english: I’ve exceeded my cash-withdrawal limit.
context: ATM PROBLEMS — ATM problem: you have reached/exceeded the daily or periodic cash-withdrawal limit.

foreign: Vous pouvez ouvrir une réclamation ?
english: Can you open a claim/complaint?
context: ATM PROBLEMS — ATM problem: asking the bank to open a formal complaint/claim about the transaction.

foreign: Je crois que j’ai fait le virement à la mauvaise personne.
english: I think I transferred the money to the wrong person.
context: BANK TRANSFER TO THE WRONG PERSON — Bank transfer mistake: you think you sent money to the wrong person/payee.

foreign: T’as mis quel IBAN ?
english: Which IBAN did you use?
context: BANK TRANSFER TO THE WRONG PERSON — Bank transfer mistake: checking which account IBAN was used.

foreign: J’ai sélectionné le mauvais bénéficiaire.
english: I selected the wrong payee.
context: BANK TRANSFER TO THE WRONG PERSON — Bank transfer mistake: you selected the wrong saved beneficiary/payee.

foreign: Il est encore possible de l’annuler ?
english: Is it still possible to cancel it?
context: BANK TRANSFER TO THE WRONG PERSON — Bank transfer mistake: asking whether the transfer can still be cancelled.

foreign: Quelle démarche je dois faire pour tenter de récupérer les fonds ?
english: What do I need to do to try to recover the funds?
context: BANK TRANSFER TO THE WRONG PERSON — Bank transfer mistake: asking the bank how to try to recover money already sent to the wrong account.

foreign: C’est quoi ce prélèvement de 6,99 ?
english: What is this €6.99 direct debit?

foreign: Ça passe tous les mois.
english: It comes out every month.

foreign: Tu paies ça depuis sept ans ?
english: You’ve been paying this for seven years?
context: SUBSCRIPTIONS FROM THE PREHISTORIC ERA — Forgotten subscription: realising you have unknowingly paid for it for seven years.

foreign: Je trouve même plus mon compte.
english: I can’t even find my account anymore.
context: SUBSCRIPTIONS FROM THE PREHISTORIC ERA — Forgotten subscription: you cannot even find the old service/account you are still being charged for.

foreign: Essaie « mot de passe oublié ».
english: Try “forgot password”.
context: SUBSCRIPTIONS FROM THE PREHISTORIC ERA — Forgotten subscription: trying the account's 'forgot password' option so you can regain access and cancel it.

foreign: J’ai encore un vieux stockage cloud.
english: I’m still paying for an old cloud-storage service.
context: SUBSCRIPTIONS FROM THE PREHISTORIC ERA — Forgotten subscription: you are still paying for an old cloud-storage service you no longer really use.

foreign: Je vais faire le ménage dans mes abonnements.
english: I’m going to clean up my subscriptions.
context: SUBSCRIPTIONS FROM THE PREHISTORIC ERA — Forgotten subscriptions: reviewing recurring subscriptions and cancelling the ones you no longer need.

english: Wait… what is this €480 direct debit tomorrow?
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment shock: you have just noticed a large €480 direct debit due tomorrow.

foreign: C’est annuel, ce truc ?
english: Is this thing annual?
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment shock: checking whether the unexpectedly large charge is yearly rather than monthly.

foreign: Je croyais que c’était mensuel.
english: I thought it was monthly.
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment shock: you had assumed the service was billed monthly.

foreign: Putain, j’avais oublié que ça tombait ce mois-ci.
english: Fuck, I’d forgotten that was coming out this month.
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment shock: you had forgotten the yearly charge was due this month.

foreign: Faut que je mette ça dans le calendrier.
english: I need to put that in the calendar.
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment planning: putting the yearly bill in the calendar so it does not surprise you next time.

english: Next year I’ll put money aside every month.
context: THE ANNUAL PAYMENT — Annual-payment planning: deciding to save a little each month for next year's yearly bill.

foreign: Je vais lisser ça sur l’année.
english: I’m going to spread that cost over the year.

context: PUTTING ASIDE FOR ANNUAL COSTS — Annual costs: spreading the yearly cost conceptually across twelve months and saving for it gradually.

foreign: Comme ça, quand ça tombe, l’argent est déjà là.
english: That way, when it comes out, the money is already there.
context: PUTTING ASIDE FOR ANNUAL COSTS — Annual costs: because you saved monthly, the money is already set aside when the yearly payment is due.

english: Would you do it for ten?

english: For five euros, I’ll take it.

foreign: À vingt, je laisse.
english: At twenty, I’ll leave it.

foreign: Moi j’ose jamais.
english: I never dare.

foreign: Mais c’est un peu le jeu.

english: Nothing, I’ve already got the money back.

english: Did the restaurant refund the deposit?

foreign: Oui, intégralement.
english: Yes, in full.

english: I’ll send your share back tonight.

english: It’s just the booking fees that aren’t refundable.

english: You paid for the restaurant.

english: But I paid for the taxi.

english: It must have made sense at the time.

english: What did you pay for?

foreign: Moi, j’ai payé quoi ?
english: What did I pay for?

foreign: Et après on fait la différence.
english: And then we work out the difference.

foreign: On devrait utiliser une appli.

english: We say that on every trip.

foreign: Ça simplifie tellement les voyages en groupe.
english: It makes group trips so much easier.

foreign: À condition que tout le monde entre ses dépenses.
english: As long as everyone enters their expenses.

foreign: Oui, donc ça marche jamais parfaitement.

english: No, make it 13.

foreign: Arrondis.
english: Round it.

foreign: Laisse, garde les centimes.

foreign: On compensera la prochaine fois.
english: We’ll make up for it next time.

foreign: Ça s’équilibre à peu près.
english: It more or less evens out.

foreign: Il propose jamais de payer.
english: He never offers to pay.

foreign: Même pas pour un café.
english: Not even for a coffee.

foreign: Il attend toujours que quelqu’un sorte sa carte.
english: He always waits for someone else to get their card out.

foreign: Ça me gêne pas de payer parfois.
english: I don’t mind paying sometimes.

foreign: Mais j’aime bien que ce soit réciproque.
english: But I like it to be reciprocal.

foreign: C’est pas une question de montant.
english: It’s not about the amount.

foreign: C’est l’intention.
english: It’s the intention.

foreign: Si quelqu’un t’invite trois fois, tu proposes au moins la quatrième.
english: If someone treats you three times, you at least offer the fourth.

foreign: Sinon ça donne une drôle d’impression.
english: Otherwise it gives a strange impression.

foreign: Elle veut toujours tout payer.
english: She always wants to pay for everything.

foreign: C’est adorable, mais ça me met presque mal à l’aise.
english: It’s lovely, but it almost makes me uncomfortable.

foreign: Je veux pouvoir l’inviter aussi.
english: I want to be able to treat her too.

foreign: Elle accepte jamais.
english: She never accepts.

foreign: La prochaine fois, je réserve et je paie avant qu’elle arrive.
english: Next time, I’ll book and pay before she arrives.

foreign: Elle est extrêmement généreuse.
english: She’s incredibly generous.

foreign: Mais je veux pas profiter.
english: But I don’t want to take advantage.

foreign: Je sais qu’elle peut se le permettre, mais c’est pas la question.
english: I know she can afford it, but that’s not the point.

foreign: Je l’aurais jamais acheté plein tarif.
english: I would never have bought it at full price.

english: No, because I’m going to spend twelve euros to save four.

foreign: Oui, dit comme ça…
english: Yeah, when you put it like that…

foreign: C’est comme ça qu’ils t’ont.
english: That’s how they get you.

foreign: Autant payer la livraison.
english: We may as well pay for delivery.

foreign: Je préfère payer pour un produit que pour la livraison.

foreign: Même quand mathématiquement ça n’a aucun sens.

foreign: Presque dix euros.

foreign: Pour un article à quinze euros ?

foreign: À ce compte-là, autant le garder.

foreign: C’est exactement ce qu’ils espèrent.

foreign: Je vais peut-être le revendre plutôt.
english: Maybe I’ll resell it instead.

english: Otherwise I just see one big sum and feel rich.

foreign: Et tu dépenses.
english: And then you spend it.

foreign: Je préfère séparer mentalement les objectifs.

foreign: Même si l’argent est techniquement au même endroit.
english: Even if the money is technically in the same place.

english: I’d like to get to €10,000 in savings.

foreign: Il te manque combien ?
english: How much are you short?

english: When do you want to get there by?

foreign: D’ici la fin de l’année.
english: By the end of the year.

foreign: C’est faisable.
english: It’s doable.

foreign: Mais faut que je sois régulière.
english: But I need to be consistent.

foreign: J’essaie de pas être trop rigide non plus.

foreign: S’il y a un mois plus cher, je mets moins.
english: If one month is more expensive, I save less.

foreign: L’important, c’est la tendance.
english: What matters is the overall trend.

foreign: J’ai enfin atteint mon objectif !
english: I’ve finally hit my target!

foreign: T’as combien maintenant ?

foreign: J’ai dépassé les 10 000.
english: I’ve passed €10,000.

foreign: Ça fait trop plaisir.

english: Wasn’t the point of saving it to use it for something?

foreign: On la reconstituera petit à petit.

foreign: Vu comme ça, ça me rassure.

foreign: C’est exactement pour ça qu’on avait mis cet argent de côté.

foreign: Il est prévu pour autre chose.

foreign: C’est pas parce qu’il y a de l’argent sur un compte que j’ai envie de le dépenser.

foreign: Cet argent a déjà un boulot.
english: That money already has a job.

foreign: Il est pour la maison.

foreign: Ou pour les imprévus.
english: Or for emergencies.

foreign: Je veux pas piocher dedans pour des achats plaisir.
english: I don’t want to dip into it for fun purchases.

foreign: Sinon ça disparaît vite.
english: Otherwise it disappears quickly.

foreign: Mes parents dépensent pas du tout comme moi.
english: My parents spend completely differently from me.

foreign: Ils gardent tout “au cas où”.
english: They keep everything ‘just in case’.

foreign: Ils détestent jeter.
english: They hate throwing things away.

foreign: Ils réparent tout.
english: They repair everything.

foreign: Ils changent rien tant que ça marche.
english: They don’t replace anything as long as it still works.

foreign: Après, ils ont grandi dans un autre contexte.
english: Then again, they grew up in a different context.

foreign: Ça marque ton rapport à l’argent.
english: That shapes your relationship with money.

foreign: Ma mère trouve déjà 20 euros cher pour certains trucs.
english: My mum already thinks €20 is expensive for some things.

foreign: Et elle peut mettre énormément dans autre chose.
english: And she can spend a huge amount on something else.

foreign: “Une baguette, ça devrait coûter 80 centimes.”
english: ‘A baguette should cost 80 cents.’

foreign: Maman, malheureusement, j’ai des nouvelles.
english: Mum, unfortunately I have news.

foreign: Tu te rappelles quand un café coûtait un euro ?
english: Do you remember when a coffee cost one euro?

foreign: Oui, me fais pas ça.
english: Yes, don’t do this to me.

foreign: Et le kebab à cinq euros ?
english: And a kebab was five euros?

foreign: Et les places de concert à vingt balles ?
english: And concert tickets were twenty euros?

foreign: J’ai encore les anciens prix dans la tête.
english: I still have the old prices in my head.

foreign: À chaque fois je trouve tout hors de prix.
english: So every time, I think everything is outrageously expensive.

foreign: Parce que mon cerveau vit encore en 2012.
english: Because my brain is still living in 2012.

foreign: Les concerts sont devenus super chers.
english: Concerts have become really expensive.

foreign: 70 euros la place, ça commence à faire.
english: €70 a ticket is starting to be a lot.

foreign: Et après tu rajoutes les frais.
english: And then you add the fees.

foreign: Et le transport.
english: And transport.

foreign: Et deux verres à dix euros.
english: And two drinks at €10 each.

foreign: La soirée te revient à 150 balles.
english: The evening ends up costing you €150.

foreign: Les festivals, j’en parle même pas.
english: Don’t even get me started on festivals.

foreign: Le pass est déjà cher.
english: The pass is already expensive.

foreign: Puis faut dormir quelque part.
english: Then you need somewhere to sleep.

foreign: Et manger.
english: And food.

foreign: Et boire.
english: And drink.

foreign: Mais si j’adore vraiment l’artiste, je mets le prix.
english: But if I really love the artist, I’ll pay the price.

foreign: Je préfère faire moins de concerts mais choisir ceux que je veux vraiment voir.
english: I’d rather go to fewer concerts and choose the ones I really want to see.

foreign: Dix euros la bière ?
english: Ten euros for a beer?

foreign: Ils savent que t’as pas le choix une fois dedans.
english: They know you have no choice once you’re inside.

foreign: Tu peux même pas sortir acheter ailleurs.
english: You can’t even leave to buy somewhere else.

foreign: Je prends de l’eau.
english: I’ll have water.

foreign: L’eau est à cinq euros.
english: The water is five euros.

foreign: Achète rien à l’aéroport, ça coûte trois fois le prix.
english: Don’t buy anything at the airport; it costs three times as much.

foreign: J’ai oublié ma bouteille d’eau.
english: I forgot my water bottle.

foreign: Combien le sandwich ?
english: How much is the sandwich?

foreign: Douze euros.
english: Twelve euros.

foreign: Je préfère mourir de faim.
english: I’d rather starve.

foreign: On aurait dû acheter avant de passer la sécurité.
english: We should have bought something before going through security.

foreign: On peut remplir la gourde quelque part ?
english: Is there somewhere we can fill the water bottle?

foreign: Je vais pas payer quatre euros pour une petite bouteille d’eau.
english: I’m not paying four euros for a small bottle of water.

foreign: Enfin… si, parce qu’on a soif.
english: Well… yes I am, because we’re thirsty.

foreign: Ils nous tiennent.
english: They’ve got us.

foreign: Ta banque prend des frais à l’étranger ?
english: Does your bank charge fees abroad?

foreign: Ils prennent une commission sur chaque paiement ?
english: Do they charge a commission on every payment?

foreign: J’utilise une carte sans frais à l’étranger.
english: I use a card with no foreign-transaction fees.

foreign: Ça évite les mauvaises surprises.
english: It avoids nasty surprises.

foreign: Tu veux payer en euros ou en monnaie locale ?
english: Do you want to pay in euros or in the local currency?

foreign: Toujours en monnaie locale.
english: Always in the local currency.

foreign: Sinon leur conversion est souvent pourrie.
english: Otherwise their exchange rate is often terrible.

foreign: J’ai appris ça après m’être fait avoir une fois.
english: I learned that after getting caught out once.

foreign: Ça fait combien en euros ?
english: How much is that in euros?

foreign: Attends, je convertis.
english: Hang on, I’ll convert it.

foreign: À peu près 40.
english: About €40.

foreign: Ah ça va.
english: Oh, that’s fine.

foreign: Non attends, j’ai mal calculé.
english: No, wait, I calculated it wrong.

foreign: C’est 70.
J’arrive jamais à savoir si je dépense beaucoup quand je comprends pas intuitivement la monnaie.
english: I can never tell whether I’m spending a lot when I don’t intuitively understand the currency.

foreign: T’as l’impression que c’est de l’argent Monopoly.
english: It feels like Monopoly money.

foreign: Il te reste des dollars ?
english: Do you have any dollars left?

foreign: Oui, genre 30.
english: Yeah, about 30.

foreign: Tu les changes ?
english: Are you going to exchange them?

foreign: Ça vaut même pas le coup avec les frais.
english: It’s not even worth it once you include the fees.

foreign: Garde-les pour la prochaine fois.
english: Keep them for next time.

foreign: “La prochaine fois” dans quinze ans.
english: ‘Next time’ in fifteen years.

foreign: J’ai encore des billets de trois pays différents chez moi.
english: I still have banknotes from three different countries at home.

Apparemment pour le ménage.

english: Are they refunding automatically?
